phase: 31-stable-release (policy first decided in phase 30-first-run-polish, unchanged since); product_version/debian_version bumped to 1.2.0 in the v1.2.0 release prep (portable Windows/macOS artifacts added; Linux package policy itself unchanged)
debian_version_mapping_rule: replace every '-' with '~' (CMakeLists.txt: string(REPLACE "-" "~" ...) applied to MEMBRANE_VERSION from tools/membrane-run/product_cli.h) -- Debian Policy 5.6.12, so a prerelease always sorts before its eventual stable release. A stable version has no hyphen, so the rule is a no-op here: '0.3.0' in, '0.3.0' out (confirmed directly: the built package's own Version: field reads exactly '0.3.0', no ~rc suffix).

decision.summary: The Vulkan-enabled build (membrane, built with -DGGML_VULKAN=ON) is the ONE official Linux amd64 .deb. It runs correctly CPU-only by default and adds exactly one extra real runtime dependency (libvulkan1) over a CPU-only build.
options_considered: A: publish only the Vulkan-enabled package as the official amd64 .deb (chosen)
B: publish CPU and Vulkan variants with distinct artifact filenames, both official
C: use separate Debian package names for both, both official
decision.chosen: A, with the CPU-only variant kept as a non-official (CI-validation/build-your-own) artifact under a distinct package name -- not published as a release asset, but not deleted either (Section 15/16: filenames/Package: names must never collide or overwrite silently, whether official or not)
decision.why: Simplest honest user experience (Section 2): one package name for the one thing most users should install, with real (not hand-waved) evidence that it degrades gracefully with no GPU. A second official artifact would only exist to shave one dependency line off a package that already works fine without a GPU -- not worth the two-download decision it would force on every user.
proof: runs correctly CPU-only: real generation completed inside a container with no GPU device visible, using the Vulkan-enabled package (results/distribution/validation.json, results/first-run/validation.json)
behaves correctly with libvulkan1 present but zero visible GPU devices: apt-installed cleanly, --list-devices reported CPU only, no crash, no hang
--doctor handles zero visible devices correctly: reports one honest combined [WARN] (Phase 29's own fix, re-verified this phase), never falsely claims 'no GPU backend compiled in' on this exact build
default invocation stays CPU-only unless GPU is requested: --gpu-layers defaults to 0 unconditionally; --auto only offloads if a device is actually found; no code path enables GPU offload implicitly
decision.never_claim: This is NOT a claim of universal Linux support. Scope: Debian-family (Ubuntu/Pop!_OS/Debian), amd64 only, libvulkan1 runtime dependency, CPU fallback available, Vulkan GPU usage optional and opt-in. No Fedora/RPM, Arch, Flatpak, Snap, AppImage, macOS, or Windows claim exists anywhere in this project's docs.
